summary: The change adds a process-local facts cache keyed by API base, credential, owner and name, re-reads the default-branch commit SHA on each lookup, reuses successful facts only when that SHA matches, and caps workflow file reads at 10 while treating an incomplete negative scan as unavailable. The added tests cover concurrent reuse, SHA changes, credential and base isolation, gating, and the 27-target reload lifecycle. No actionable defect was found.

evidence: The resolver reads GET /repos/{owner}/{name}/commits/{defaultBranch} and rejects a missing or non-40-hex SHA before any contents read (src/host/target-tree-facts.ts:323-334).

Successful facts are cached in the process map `treeFactsByRun`, keyed by API base, token, owner and name, and reused only when the freshly read SHA matches the cached SHA (src/host/target-tree-facts.ts:49-60, 336-355).
Workflow reads are capped at `MAX_WORKFLOW_FILES = 10`; an incomplete negative scan returns `null` instead of falsely reporting no PR CI (src/host/target-tree-facts.ts:225-247).

The new 27-target lifecycle test asserts that a reload with unchanged default-branch SHAs performs no extra contents reads, while changed heads reload pinned facts (tests/host/target-tree-facts_test.ts:260-313).
